layers.mission: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, with Mars Express
layers.instrument: HiRISE, with CTX and HRSC images where HiRISE was lacking
layers.realDetail: About 25 to 32 cm where from HiRISE; objects need to be about 1 m across to be recognised
layers.positionAccuracy: About 100 m: tied to MOLA through HRSC (product page). Curiosity's stops are placed on this same mosaic
caveats: Taken between 2006 and 2011, before Curiosity reached this area. Rover tracks are not in it, and sand may have moved.
Lit by the afternoon Sun at the time of each image. Dark patches can be shadows, not dark ground.
One black-and-white band. It shows brightness, not colour.
layers.title: Ground from orbit
layers.processing: Cut to the site's box and redrawn as map tiles for zoom 12 to 18. One tile pixel at zoom 18 is 0.32 m on the ground. Places with no data are transparent.

layers.mission: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, with Mars Express and Mars Global Surveyor
layers.instrument: HiRISE stereo, with CTX and HRSC terrain where HiRISE stereo was lacking, tied to MOLA
layers.realDetail: About 3 to 5 m where made from HiRISE stereo; far coarser where CTX or HRSC terrain fills a gap
layers.positionAccuracy: About 100 m: tied to MOLA through HRSC, which is only as accurate as MOLA (product page). Curiosity's stops are placed on this same mosaic
caveats: Rocks, ledges and ripples smaller than about 3 to 5 m are not in this model, and the boxwork ridges, about 1 to 2 m tall, are smaller than that.
Where HiRISE stereo was lacking the mosaic used CTX, HRSC or MOLA terrain, which is coarser. The page does not map where.
Made from images taken between 2006 and 2011, before Curiosity reached this area.
For 400 m round the box the 3D ground is eased down to the box's lowest point so the box does not stand up as a block; that edge is not measured terrain.
layers.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona/ESA/DLR/FU Berlin/USGS (Calef and Parker 2016)
layers.title: Terrain height
layers.processing: Cut to the site's box and stored as height tiles for zoom 11 to 15, to the nearest 0.1 m. One tile pixel at zoom 15 is 2.5 m on the ground, so the 3D view is smoother than the 1 m grid. Past the edge of the box the edge heights are eased down to the box's lowest point over 400 m, because the map has no terrain beyond it; that easing is for the picture only and is not data. Routes and slopes use only the terrain inside the box.

layers.mission: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, with Mars Express and Mars Global Surveyor
layers.instrument: HiRISE stereo, with CTX and HRSC terrain where HiRISE stereo was lacking, tied to MOLA
layers.gridSpacing: 4 m cells, each holding the steepest of 16 slopes measured on the 1 m terrain
layers.realDetail: About 6 m: each slope is measured over 6.0 m north to south and 5.979 m east to west
layers.positionAccuracy: About 100 m: tied to MOLA through HRSC, which is only as accurate as MOLA (product page). Curiosity's stops are placed on this same mosaic
caveats: Rocks, ledges and ripples smaller than about 3 to 5 m are not in this model, and the boxwork ridges, about 1 to 2 m tall, are smaller than that.
Where HiRISE stereo was lacking the mosaic used CTX, HRSC or MOLA terrain, which is coarser. The page does not map where.
Made from images taken between 2006 and 2011, before Curiosity reached this area.
Checked against the tilt the rover measured at 285 stops: typical difference 2.3 degrees, 9 in 10 within 6.6 degrees. Rover drivers choose gentle ground, so steep slopes are less well checked.
A short steep step, such as a ledge under about 3 m, can be missed.
layers.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona/ESA/DLR/FU Berlin/USGS (Calef and Parker 2016)
layers.title: Slope
layers.processing: Steepest slope at each 1 m cell of the terrain, then the steepest of those in each routing cell. Cells are narrower east to west at this latitude and the spacing is corrected for it.

layers.title: Rover stops
layers.instrument: Curiosity rover: the rover team's own position for each drive
layers.published: A live file that grows as the rover drives; our copy ends at sol 5070
layers.gridSpacing: One point where each drive ended
layers.realDetail: A single position for each stop
layers.processing: Cut to the site's box. Positions are as the rover team published them; nothing is moved or smoothed. Earth dates are the UTC date of local midday on each sol.
caveats: The file does not say how accurate these positions are.
Where a rover drove is not proof that a person on foot can walk there, and the reverse.
Only the part inside this site's box is shown.
